If you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle your privacy differently? Most of us would. We'd be more careful about which services we use and what information we share. Since a time machine doesn't exist, we have to face reality—your personal data is being bought and sold publicly.

Right now, your phone number, email address, home address, and even family relationships are being packaged and sold to marketing companies, insurance firms, and hackers. While Safari and Mail's built-in Apple privacy protections can block some tracking as you browse, they can't retrieve data that has been collected over the years and scattered across hundreds of broker databases. Data brokers have built a multi-billion-dollar industry by harvesting your digital information, packaging it, and selling it. It's time to pull your personal data off the market and the internet. Let's look at how.

The security risks of the data broker industry

However, the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your data is everywhere, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyber threats. Because this industry is virtually unregulated, your most private information and details—including former employers and old addresses, past loan records, and more—are available for purchase at any time. This poses a significant security concern.

Modern scammers leverage broker data to carefully craft highly personalized (and hard-to-spot) phishing attacks. When scammers already know your job title, home address, and even the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your instinctive defenses. If a scammer knows you inside and out, they only need to strike when your guard is down to dramatically increase their chances of success.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function as openly searchable databases, becoming tools for stalkers and harassers. By mapping the network of relationships between your relatives, friends, and neighbors, brokers provide a blueprint for locating people who are trying to maintain their privacy and deliberately stay under the radar.

The solution: Use Incogni to automatically remove your data

The scale of this ecosystem is staggering and frankly, demoralizing. Trying to request the deletion of your data from hundreds of websites one by one is nearly futile even if you worked on it full-time—because if it were easy, these brokers would have gone out of business long ago. What you need is a solution that understands how this industry works and knows how to defend your right to privacy.

This precisely illustrates why a service like Incogni is so important to your life—both in the digital world and the real world. This service takes your massive headache (data being everywhere and sold) and turns it into a solved problem with a one-stop approach. Incogni handles the tedious, repetitive paperwork of opt-out requests on your behalf automatically, so you don't have to spend months tracking down data brokers one by one. They ensure your data isn't just removed once, but stays deleted, preventing brokers from quietly re-collecting it.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track your personal data removal progress in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may hold your data

The real benefits of data removal for the privacy-conscious

Getting scrubbed from internet broker databases can deliver immediate benefits for you and your family

  • When companies can't buy your number, spam calls and junk texts will decrease.
  • Scammers lose their leads. Identity thieves often source their victims' information from broker sites.
  • Your personal address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to locate your home with ease.
  • Your credit score stays healthy because data exposure is limited, reducing the risk of identity theft and strengthening your overall financial health.
